title: Allow usernames that start with a digit

findings.label: intended
findings.why: The PR allows usernames starting with digits, so '1user' now passes validation and returns 201 instead of 400.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The test was changed from '1user' to '_user', but the observed error shows a new email validation error appearing that the PR description does not mention.

doppel.summary: The PR correctly allows digit-starting usernames, but an unrelated email validation error appears in the test output.

review.why: The PR intentionally relaxes the username validation to allow starting with a digit, matching the description. The test change from '1user' to '_user' preserves coverage for invalid usernames (now testing underscore prefix). No other behavior is altered.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames may now start with a letter or a digit (e.g. `2pac`).". The validation change from isalpha() to isalnum() in schemas.py allows digit-starting usernames, turning erin's PUT /api/me from 400 to 200.

findings.why: The username field appears unchanged in the truncated response bodies; the diff only modifies validation, not the returned username value.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with underscore are now rejected instead of accepted
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {'username': '_user', 'email': 'test@example.com', 'password': 'dog'}; read back 400 status and validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s1 sent POST /api/users with username '_user' and both base and head returned 400 with validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with non-alphanumeric characters (e.g. @, #, $) are now rejected instead of accepted
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {'username': '@user', 'email': 'test@example.com', 'password': 'dog'}; read back 400 status and validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s2 sent POST /api/users with username '@user' and both base and head returned 400 with validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with unicode letters outside ASCII may be rejected due to isalnum() behavior
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {'username': 'élise', 'email': 'test@example.com', 'password': 'dog'}; read back 400 status and validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s3 sent POST /api/users with username 'élise' and both base and head returned 400 with validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with unicode digits outside ASCII may be rejected due to isalnum() behavior
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {'username': '١user', 'email': 'test@example.com', 'password': 'dog'}; read back 400 status and validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s4 sent POST /api/users with username '١user' and both base and head returned 400 with validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'.

suspicions.claim: Empty username string causes IndexError crash instead of validation error
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {'username': '', 'email': 'test@example.com', 'password': 'dog'}; read back 500 status or IndexError in response
suspicions.evidence: Probe s5 sent POST /api/users with empty username and both base and head returned 400 with validation error, not 500 or IndexError.

suspicions.claim: Username update via PUT /api/me now allows digit-starting usernames but may reject previously valid unicode-starting usernames
suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as existing user, send PUT /api/me with JSON {'username': '2newname'}; read back 200 success. Then send PUT /api/me with JSON {'username': 'élise'}; read back 400 validation error
suspicions.evidence: Probe s6 authenticated and sent PUT /api/me with username '2newname'; base returned 400, head returned 200 (f1, f3). Error message changed from 'must start with a letter' to 'must start with a letter or digit' (f5).
